2_Introduction: The device displayed a champion PCE of 19.6547%, with a VOC of 1.1021 V, a JSC of 23.776 mA/cm², and an FF of 75.0033%. The composition of perovskite is 1.73 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. With 6 s of spin time remaining, CB (160 µL) was dispensed onto the middle of the substrate. An annealing process at 110 °C for 25 min allowed the perovskite grains to fully mature.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ with a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture, achieves an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) that suppresses δ-phase formation while enhancing thermal and phase stability; the low Br⁻ content (10% on X-site) minimally widens the bandgap yet critically passivates halide vacancies and mitigates iodide-mediated ion migration, whereas the precise precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) for uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 30 s) crystallization under controlled antisolvent dripping (160 µL chlorobenzene introduced at the 24 s mark, i.e., 6 s before spin cessation)—enables rapid nucleation suppression and extended grain growth kinetics, yielding large, oriented grains with reduced intragrain strain and suppressed interfacial trap states; this crystallization orchestration, further consolidated by the 110 °C/25 min annealing step, promotes complete solvent evaporation, PbI₂ residual phase elimination (as confirmed by absent XRD peaks at ~12.6°), and full conversion to the desired α-phase, evidenced by sharp, narrow XRD (001) and (011) reflections with minimal FWHM—indicative of high crystallinity and low microstrain—as well as uniform film coverage and high grayscale homogeneity in optical microscopy, reflecting nanoscale morphological continuity and absence of pinholes or dewetting features that would otherwise create shunting pathways; concurrently, the spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity and monoexponential decay profile with prolonged lifetime (>1.2 µs) directly corroborate effective suppression of non-radiative recombination centers across the entire film area, consistent with both bulk and surface defect passivation arising from intrinsic compositional engineering (e.g., FA⁺-induced lattice rigidity, Cs⁺-mediated grain boundary stabilization, and Br⁻-assisted halide vacancy filling) and extrinsic processing control (e.g., antisolvent-induced intermediate phase templating and thermal annealing-driven defect healing); collectively, these structural, morphological, and optoelectronic signatures—jointly validated by XRD phase purity, image-derived film uniformity, and PL-derived carrier lifetime enhancement—underpin efficient charge extraction, minimized interfacial recombination, and balanced electron/hole transport, culminating in a champion device delivering VOC = 1.1021 V, JSC = 23.776 mA/cm², FF = 75.0033%, and PCE = 19.6547%.
